from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Mystery of the Speed Trap", [
            "Dash the cheetah sprints 100 meters in 4 seconds.",
            "His average speed is exactly 25 meters per second.",
            "We freeze-frame his journey at exactly 2.5 seconds.",
            "Look closely at the position of his paws now.",
            "How fast is he moving at this specific instant?"
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Dash the cheetah sprints 100 meters in 4 seconds.
        # Color: Yellow (#FFFF00)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        dash = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(dash, "C1")
        
        path_start = self.grid["C1"]
        path_end = self.grid["C6"]
        
        # Use ValueTracker for horizontal movement
        pos_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        dash.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(path_start + pos_tracker.get_value() * (path_end - path_start)))
        
        self.add(dash)
        self.play(pos_tracker.animate(run_time=3, rate_func=linear).set_value(1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # His average speed is exactly 25 meters per second.
        # Color: White (#FFFFFF)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        avg_speed_label = Text("Average Speed = 25 m/s", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_in_area(avg_speed_label, "D1", "D6")
        
        self.play(Write(avg_speed_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # We freeze-frame his journey at exactly 2.5 seconds.
        # Color: Cyan (#00FFFF)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # Reset dash for the freeze-frame demonstration
        self.play(pos_tracker.animate(run_time=0.5).set_value(0))
        
        # 2.5 seconds out of 4 seconds = 0.625 of the total path
        freeze_point = 0.625
        
        # Vertical cyan line at the 2.5s position
        # Calculate horizontal position based on interpolation between C1 and C6
        freeze_x = self.grid["C1"][0] + freeze_point * (self.grid["C6"][0] - self.grid["C1"][0])
        freeze_line = Line(
            start=[freeze_x, self.grid["B1"][1], 0],
            end=[freeze_x, self.grid["D1"][1], 0],
            color="#00FFFF",
            stroke_width=4
        )
        
        self.play(pos_tracker.animate(run_time=1.875, rate_func=linear).set_value(freeze_point))
        self.play(Create(freeze_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Look closely at the position of his paws now.
        # Color: White (#FFFFFF)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # White circle to focus on "paws" (bottom of the circle)
        focus_circle = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=4)
        focus_circle.move_to(dash.get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(focus_circle))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # How fast is he moving at this specific instant?
        # Color: Magenta (#FF00FF)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        question_mark = Text("?", font_size=48, color="#FF00FF")
        # Place roughly above the frozen dash (around column 4)
        self.place_at_grid(question_mark, "B4") 
        
        # Flashing effect
        def flashing_effect(m, dt):
            m.set_opacity(0.5 + 0.5 * np.sin(self.time * 10))

        self.add(question_mark)
        question_mark.add_updater(flashing_effect)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(question_mark))
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Clean up updaters
        dash.remove_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(path_start + pos_tracker.get_value() * (path_end - path_start)))
        question_mark.remove_updater(flashing_effect)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching content from storyboard
        title_text = "The Curved Path Problem"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Curves represent things that change speed over time.",
            "At any point, the steepness is constantly shifting.",
            "Our standard slope formula needs two points, not one."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup visualization elements
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[0, 3, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "stroke_width": 2},
            tips=False
        )
        # Function: y = 0.2 * x^2
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * x**2, color=WHITE)
        
        plot_group = VGroup(axes, curve)
        self.place_in_area(plot_group, "B1", "E6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Value tracker for car position along x-axis
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(-2.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Curves represent things that change speed over time."
        # A white (#FFFFFF) curve representing a parabola y = 0.2x^2 appears.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "At any point, the steepness is constantly shifting."
        # A cyan (#00FFFF) small rectangle moves along the curve to simulate a car.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(CYAN)
        
        # Car mobject (Polygon to ensure robust updates of points)
        car = Polygon(
            np.array([-0.2, -0.1, 0]),
            np.array([0.2, -0.1, 0]),
            np.array([0.2, 0.1, 0]),
            np.array([-0.2, 0.1, 0]),
            color=CYAN, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=2
        )
        
        def update_car(obj):
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            center = axes.c2p(t, 0.2 * t**2)
            # Calculate local slope for orientation
            dt = 0.01
            p1 = axes.c2p(t, 0.2 * t**2)
            p2 = axes.c2p(t + dt, 0.2 * (t + dt)**2)
            direction = p2 - p1
            angle = np.arctan2(direction[1], direction[0])
            
            # Point-based rotation to avoid accumulation issues
            w, h = 0.4, 0.2
            base_corners = [
                np.array([-w/2, -h/2, 0]),
                np.array([w/2, -h/2, 0]),
                np.array([w/2, h/2, 0]),
                np.array([-w/2, h/2, 0]),
            ]
            rot_matrix = np.array([
                [np.cos(angle), -np.sin(angle), 0],
                [np.sin(angle), np.cos(angle), 0],
                [0, 0, 1]
            ])
            rotated_corners = [center + np.dot(rot_matrix, c) for c in base_corners]
            obj.set_points_as_corners([*rotated_corners, rotated_corners[0]])

        car.add_updater(update_car)
        self.play(FadeIn(car))
        # Animate movement halfway to show progress
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(0), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Our standard slope formula needs two points, not one."
        # A yellow (#FFFF00) line segment follows the car, showing changing steepness.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        tangent_line = Line(color=YELLOW, stroke_width=5)
        
        def update_tangent(obj):
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            center = axes.c2p(t, 0.2 * t**2)
            dt = 0.01
            p1 = axes.c2p(t, 0.2 * t**2)
            p2 = axes.c2p(t + dt, 0.2 * (t + dt)**2)
            direction = p2 - p1
            direction_norm = np.linalg.norm(direction)
            if direction_norm == 0:
                return
            direction /= direction_norm
            
            # Visually consistent tangent segment length
            line_length = 1.6
            obj.set_points_as_corners([
                center - direction * (line_length / 2),
                center + direction * (line_length / 2)
            ])
            
        tangent_line.add_updater(update_tangent)
        self.play(Create(tangent_line))
        
        # Finish the movement to demonstrate changing slope
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(2.5), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup layout using storyboard data
        title = "The Secant Line Bridge"
        lecture_lines = [
            "A secant line connects two points on a curve.",
            "Its slope approximates the speed between these two moments.",
            "But this average is still just a blurry guess."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors from storyboard
        COLOR_CURVE = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_POINT_Q = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_SECANT = "#FFFF00"
        
        # 2. Prepare graph elements
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 3, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "include_numbers": False},
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            tips=True
        ).set_color(GRAY)
        
        # Curve y = x^2
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[0, 2.2], color=COLOR_CURVE)
        
        # Point P at (1,1)
        p_coords = axes.c2p(1, 1)
        point_p = Dot(p_coords, color=COLOR_CURVE)
        label_p = MathTex("P(1,1)", font_size=20, color=COLOR_CURVE).next_to(point_p, DOWN + LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Point Q at (2,4)
        q_coords = axes.c2p(2, 4)
        point_q = Dot(q_coords, color=COLOR_POINT_Q)
        label_q = MathTex("Q(2,4)", font_size=20, color=COLOR_POINT_Q).next_to(point_q, UP + LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Secant Line connecting P and Q
        secant_line = Line(p_coords, q_coords, color=COLOR_SECANT)
        
        # Slope Label
        slope_label = MathTex(r"\text{Slope} = 3", font_size=22, color=COLOR_SECANT)
        slope_label.next_to(secant_line.get_center(), RIGHT, buff=0.2)

        # Group and position in the 6x6 grid area
        graph_group = VGroup(axes, curve, point_p, label_p, point_q, label_q, secant_line, slope_label)
        self.place_in_area(graph_group, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Initially hide elements to animate them step-by-step
        self.remove(graph_group)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "A secant line connects two points on a curve."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_CURVE))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.play(FadeIn(point_p), Write(label_p))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Its slope approximates the speed between these two moments."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_POINT_Q))
        self.play(FadeIn(point_q), Write(label_q))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "But this average is still just a blurry guess."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_SECANT))
        self.play(Create(secant_line))
        self.play(Write(slope_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Let's slide point Q closer to our target P.",
            "The gap between them, called h, shrinks toward zero.",
            "As Q approaches P, the secant line starts tilting.",
            "It transforms into a tangent line touching one point.",
            "This limit reveals the exact speed at point P."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Limit: Zooming into Infinity", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup axes and curve
        # Area A1 to F6 covers the right side
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 2.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 6.5, 1],
            x_length=3.8,
            y_length=4.0,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY_B}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[0, 2.4], color=BLUE)
        
        # Point P is fixed at x=1
        x_p = 1
        y_p = x_p**2
        p_point = Dot(axes.c2p(x_p, y_p), color=WHITE)
        p_label = MathTex("P", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        p_label.next_to(p_point, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # h Tracker to move Point Q
        h_tracker = ValueTracker(1.2) # Initial distance from P
        
        # Point Q (#00FF00) slides down the curve toward point P (#FFFFFF)
        q_point = Dot(color="#00FF00")
        q_point.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(axes.c2p(x_p + h_tracker.get_value(), (x_p + h_tracker.get_value())**2)))
        
        q_label = MathTex("Q", color="#00FF00", font_size=24)
        q_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(q_point, RIGHT, buff=0.1))

        # Yellow (#FFFF00) secant line rotates to track the moving point Q
        secant_line = Line(color=YELLOW)
        def update_secant(m):
            h = h_tracker.get_value()
            if h < 0.02:
                m.set_color("#00FF00")
                # Tangent line at x=1: y = 2x - 1. Points from x=0.4 to 2.2
                p1 = axes.c2p(0.4, 2*0.4 - 1)
                p2 = axes.c2p(2.4, 2*2.4 - 1)
                m.set_points_as_corners([p1, p2])
            else:
                m.set_color(YELLOW)
                # Secant through (1,1) and (1+h, (1+h)^2). Slope m_s = ( (1+h)^2 - 1 ) / h = 2+h
                m_s = 2 + h
                p1 = axes.c2p(0.4, m_s*(0.4 - x_p) + y_p)
                p2 = axes.c2p(2.4, m_s*(2.4 - x_p) + y_p)
                m.set_points_as_corners([p1, p2])
        
        secant_line.add_updater(update_secant)
        
        # White (#FFFFFF) text label shows the slope value decreasing towards 2.
        slope_label = Text("Slope:", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_label, "A4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        slope_val = DecimalNumber(2 + 1.2, num_decimal_places=2, color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        slope_val.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_value(2 + h_tracker.get_value()))
        slope_val.next_to(slope_label, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        # Cyan (#00FFFF) horizontal bracket shows the distance 'h' shrinking to zero.
        h_bracket = always_redraw(lambda: 
            BraceBetweenPoints(axes.c2p(x_p, -0.2), axes.c2p(x_p + h_tracker.get_value(), -0.2), color="#00FFFF")
            if h_tracker.get_value() > 0.05 else Line(axes.c2p(x_p, -0.2), axes.c2p(x_p, -0.2), stroke_width=0)
        )
        
        h_label = MathTex("h", color="#00FFFF", font_size=24)
        h_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(h_bracket, DOWN, buff=0.1))

        # Setup Scene
        self.add(axes, curve, p_point, p_label, q_point, q_label, secant_line, slope_label, slope_val)
        
        # Reset for animation sequence
        self.remove(axes, curve, p_point, p_label, q_point, q_label, secant_line, slope_label, slope_val)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), FadeIn(p_point), FadeIn(p_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(q_point), FadeIn(q_label), Create(secant_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(h_bracket), FadeIn(h_label), FadeIn(slope_label), FadeIn(slope_val))
        self.play(h_tracker.animate.set_value(0.6), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(h_tracker.animate.set_value(0.2), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(h_tracker.animate.set_value(0.01), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(h_tracker.animate.set_value(0), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_text = "Real-World Application: Beyond Speed"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Derivatives measure change in more than just physical movement.",
            "They accurately predict power draw in your smartphone battery.",
            "Calculus is the language of our constantly changing world."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Initialization of variables
        fill_width_tracker = ValueTracker(3.8) # Initial width of the battery fill

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A white (#FFFFFF) battery icon outline appears on the screen.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        battery_outline = Rectangle(width=4, height=2, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=4)
        battery_tip = Rectangle(width=0.4, height=0.8, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=4, fill_opacity=0)
        battery_tip.next_to(battery_outline, RIGHT, buff=0)
        
        battery_group = VGroup(battery_outline, battery_tip)
        self.place_in_area(battery_group, "B2", "E5")
        
        self.play(Create(battery_outline), Create(battery_tip), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # A green (#00FF00) fill inside the battery slowly moves to the left.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#888888")
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Setup battery fill with updater for smooth width changes
        battery_fill = Rectangle(
            width=3.8,
            height=1.8,
            fill_color="#00FF00",
            fill_opacity=0.8,
            stroke_width=0
        ).move_to(battery_outline.get_center())
        
        # Correctly align fill inside the outline
        battery_fill.align_to(battery_outline, LEFT).shift(RIGHT * 0.1)
        
        # Persistent updater for stretching the fill
        battery_fill.add_updater(
            lambda m: m.stretch_to_fit_width(
                max(0.01, fill_width_tracker.get_value()), 
                about_edge=LEFT
            )
        )
        
        self.add(battery_fill)
        # Slowly decrease the battery level
        self.play(fill_width_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # A yellow (#FFFF00) arrow points to the decreasing edge, labeled 'Power Draw'.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#888888")
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Create persistent arrow and label
        arrow = Arrow(
            start=UP * 0.8, 
            end=ORIGIN, 
            color="#FFFF00", 
            buff=0.1,
            stroke_width=5,
            max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.3
        )
        
        # Label created once outside updater
        label = Text("Power Draw", font_size=20, color="#FFFF00")
        
        # Updater to keep arrow pointing to the moving edge
        def update_arrow(m):
            left_x = battery_outline.get_left()[0] + 0.1
            current_x = left_x + fill_width_tracker.get_value()
            # Position arrow above the fill's right edge
            m.move_to(np.array([current_x, battery_outline.get_top()[1] + 0.5, 0]))

        arrow.add_updater(update_arrow)
        label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(arrow, UP, buff=0.1))
        
        self.play(Create(arrow), Write(label))
        
        # Continue draining the battery while the arrow follows
        self.play(fill_width_tracker.animate.set_value(0.2), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Secret of Speed: Understanding Instantaneous Rate of Change & The Derivative
outline.target_audience: High school seniors or first-year university students (Introductory Calculus)

sections.title: The Mystery of the Speed Trap
sections.content: Introduction to the concept of 'speed at a single moment' versus 'average speed'. Contrast the total journey of a character with a specific moment in time to spark curiosity about how math captures a single instant.
sections.example: A cheetah (named Dash) sprints 100 meters in 4 seconds. While his average speed is 25m/s, we freeze-frame the video at exactly 2.5 seconds. How fast is he moving at that specific 'frozen' moment when his paws are off the ground?

sections.title: Prerequisite Check: The Slope of a Line
sections.content: Review the fundamental concept of slope (Rise over Run) on a linear graph. This establishes the foundation that rate of change is represented by the steepness of a line.
sections.example: A graph showing a steady hiker climbing a constant 30-degree slope. We calculate slope (m) = (Change in Height) / (Change in Distance). This is easy because the steepness never changes.

sections.title: The Curved Path Problem
sections.content: Transition from straight lines to curves (non-linear functions). Explain that on a curve, the 'steepness' is constantly changing, making the standard slope formula insufficient for a single point.
sections.example: Visualize a roller coaster car ascending a circular loop. At the bottom, it's flat; halfway up, it's steep. We want the slope at exactly one point P, but the slope formula requires TWO points.

sections.title: The Secant Line Bridge
sections.content: Introduce the 'Secant Line'—a line connecting point P (our target) to a nearby point Q. Show that the slope of this line is an 'average' approximation of the rate of change between those two points.
sections.example: On a graph of y = x², we place point P at (1,1) and point Q at (2,4). The line connecting them has a slope of 3. This is a 'blurry' version of the speed at point P.

sections.title: The Limit: Zooming into Infinity
sections.content: The core conceptual leap. Animate point Q sliding along the curve toward point P. As the distance (h) between their x-coordinates shrinks toward zero, the secant line transforms into the 'Tangent Line'.
sections.example: An animation shows point Q moving closer to P: (1.5, 2.25), then (1.1, 1.21), then (1.01, 1.0201). The slope of the line evolves from 3 to 2.5 to 2.1, finally settling on exactly 2 as the gap vanishes.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
sections.content: Formalize the visual process into the limit definition of the derivative. Explain that the derivative f'(x) is simply the formula that gives us the slope of the tangent line at any point.
sections.example: The mathematical notation appears over the animation: f'(x) = lim (h->0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. We show that for our cheetah's position function, the derivative tells us his exact speedometer reading at any second.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Beyond Speed
sections.content: Briefly demonstrate that derivatives apply to any system where things change, not just physical movement.
sections.example: A smartphone battery draining over time. The derivative at '3:00 PM' represents exactly how much power-draw is happening at that micro-second, allowing the OS to predict remaining life accurately.
